input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: Sharing the wrapper's statistics dictionary removes per-invocation isolation for concurrent and recursive calls. The async wrapper introduces the same regression.
- rationale: When two threads call the same decorated function, both retry copies now use the same dictionary despite having separate thread-local contexts. Starting the second call clears and resets the first call's statistics, and subsequent retries mix their counters, exposing incorrect statistics to callers. Likewise, overlapping async calls share their counters, and a recursive call overwrites the outer call's statistics.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label: the wrapper reuses one statistics dict across invocations. The second call clears and resets the first call's stats, and concurrent, async or recursive calls end up with mixed or wrong statistics.
